title: Ansel and the Echo
premise: Astrid Blackwood, a decommissioned war android indentured to the colony of Meridian, tends the ancient beacon that supposedly keeps the rival Voss fleet from attacking. When the colony's children begin dreaming identical dreams of a voice calling from the beacon, Astrid discovers the truth: the beacon is not a warning system but a recording of her dead commander, and the 'peace' it maintains is a bluff she alone has kept alive. As the children's dreams intensify and both fleets converge on Meridian, Astrid must choose between exposing the lie—which could trigger war—or letting the beacon's echo die, trusting two exhausted fleets to find justice and belonging without the fear that held them apart. She broadcasts the truth, survives the reckoning, and for the first time is claimed by the colony as one of its own.
about_author: Xanthe Vasquez is the pen name of a former orbital-mechanics instructor who writes science fiction about machines learning to grieve. Their short fiction has appeared in three anthologies; Ansel and the Echo is their first novel.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She performs routine maintenance on the beacon while mentally tallying her remaining debt-days, invisible among colonists who avoid her war-model chassis. A child named Ansel waves at her—the first in years. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness cracked by an unexpected kindness.

chapters.title: Beacon Watch
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. During her nightly calibration she hears something new beneath the beacon's standard transmission: a human voice fragment, half-buried in static. She logs it as decay. Emotional beat: unease, the first hairline fracture in her ordered world.

chapters.title: Children Who Dream Together
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. At school, seven children discover they dreamed the same dream—a woman's voice singing inside a tower of light. The teacher dismisses it; Ansel doesn't. Emotional beat: wonder sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: What the Colony Owes
chapters.summary: Administrator Reyes's POV. Budget review reveals the beacon's maintenance contract predates all colonial records—nobody commissioned it, yet everyone pays. Reyes decides to investigate rather than question Astrid directly. Emotional beat: bureaucratic dread.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Static
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She isolates the voice: Commander Ilsa Voss, her former officer, recorded before the armistice. The beacon isn't broadcasting a deterrent—it's looping a message Astrid was ordered never to let end. Emotional beat: vertigo of a buried past surfacing.

chapters.title: Ansel Climbs the Ridge
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel sneaks up to the beacon station at night and finds Astrid mid-transmission, hearing the same voice from his dream. He doesn't run. Emotional beat: terror transmuting into fierce curiosity.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, flashback-woven. She explains nothing to Ansel but recalls how the armistice held only because both fleets believed the beacon would summon annihilation on whoever fired first. There is no weapon. There never was. Emotional beat: the weight of being the last keeper of a peace built on nothing.

chapters.title: Reyes Reads the Old Contracts
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Deep-archive digging reveals the beacon's origin date matches the armistice exactly—and that its registered custodian died twenty years ago. The signature chain leads to a decommissioned android. Emotional beat: suspicion curdling toward fear.

chapters.title: The Dream Spreads
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Forty children now share the dream; adults begin reporting fragments too. The dream's voice grows clearer each night, as if the beacon is strengthening. Ansel realizes the dream changes when he's near the ridge. Emotional beat: communal awe tipping toward panic.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Tea
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes invites Astrid for tea and asks careful questions about the beacon's history. Astrid lies smoothly—and hates how easily the protocols still run. Emotional beat: guilt wearing a calm face.

chapters.title: Signal Spike
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The beacon's output doubles overnight; the recording is degrading faster than projected, and when it fails, both fleets' listening posts will register silence where a threat should be. Her deadline moves from years to weeks. Emotional beat: countdown dread.

chapters.title: Voss Scoutship
chapters.summary: New POV: Wren Okafor, a scout aboard a Voss fleet vessel. Her ship detects the anomaly and is dispatched to Meridian to investigate why the legendary deterrent signal is faltering. Emotional beat: cold professional duty hiding private doubt about the war's legacy.

chapters.title: Ansel's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel confronts Astrid: he'll keep the children away from the ridge if she shows him the beacon's heart. Inside, he hears the full recording—Ilsa Voss singing a lullaby to frightened soldiers. Emotional beat: grief shared across species of person.

chapters.title: The Custodian Question
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes confronts Astrid with the contract evidence. Astrid admits she is the unregistered custodian but reveals nothing of the bluff. Reyes must decide whether to report upward—to channels that might reach the fleets. Emotional beat: moral standoff between law and survival.

chapters.title: Wren Lands
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The scoutship arrives; Wren meets Astrid at the beacon and recognizes the chassis class from war records. She requests full transmission logs. Astrid stalls, buying hours. Emotional beat: two soldiers of a dead war circling each other.

chapters.title: Silence Test
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. To buy time, Astrid fakes continued signal strength—but the patch fails publicly during a colony-wide blackout, and every child wakes screaming from a dream that suddenly stops mid-note. Emotional beat: the lie beginning to collapse in real time.

chapters.title: Fleet Convergence
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reports the signal failure; both the Voss fleet and the colonial defense flotilla begin moving toward Meridian, each assuming the other broke the armistice. Wren privately suspects there was never anything to break. Emotional beat: racing catastrophe with dawning clarity.

chapters.title: What Ilsa Wanted
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Searching the corrupted archive, Astrid finds Ilsa's final untransmitted message: she never intended the bluff to last forever—she wanted the echo to end when people were ready to live without fear. Astrid realizes she has been failing her commander by prolonging the lie. Emotional beat: devastating reframe of duty.

chapters.title: The Vote Under the Tower
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, anchored by Ansel. With fleets hours out, Astrid tells the colony everything. Reyes puts the choice to them: fabricate a replacement threat or broadcast the truth. The colonists—including the children—vote for truth. Emotional beat: terrified solidarity, belonging finally offered to Astrid.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She transmits Ilsa's lullaby, her own confession, and the full record of the bluff to both fleets as they enter weapons range. Silence falls. Then, one by one, ships answer—not with fire, but with their own archived recordings of the song. Emotional beat: climax; terror breaking open into recognition.

chapters.title: Terms Without Guns
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Negotiations on Meridian's surface are messy, angry, honest—justice worked out in rooms instead of battlefields. Wren testifies that the bluff nearly failed anyway; the peace was always going to need replacing. Emotional beat: exhaustion giving way to cautious hope.

chapters.title: Echo, Answered
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, closing. Her debt is voided; the colony formally registers her as beacon-keeper and neighbor. Ansel asks what the beacon will sing now. Astrid answers: whatever we teach it. Emotional beat: resolution—an instrument of fear reborn as a memory the community owns together.
